claim_status: Parameter-checked reduction note only. This is not a proof of the external Alltop, Kramer-Mesner, Mendelsohn-Hung, Ostergard-Pottonen, Yoshizawa, or Keevash theorems, and it is not a full solution of #835.
main_reduction: For odd prime p > 3, Alltop extension/derivation shifts the remaining prime case from LS[p](p-2,p-1,2p-2) to LS[p](p-3,p-2,2p-3).

prime_rows.known_status: equivalent to LS[5](2,3,7); Cayley gives at most two disjoint Fano planes
derives to S(4,5,11); Kramer-Mesner gives at most two disjoint systems
derives four times to S(4,5,15), known nonexistent by Mendelsohn-Hung
derives six times to S(4,5,17), known nonexistent by Ostergard-Pottonen
derives to S(4,5,21), the first low-derived open row noted in the literature

fixed_depth_barrier.summary: For each fixed t in the checked range, LS[p](t,t+1,p+t) has p component designs and passes the usual Steiner divisibility conditions for the sampled primes p > t+1. This supports the negative strategy note: fixed-depth derived nonexistence is not a plausible global obstruction once paired with Keevash-type large-set existence theorems.
